_doc: THE MACHINE-READABLE KNOWN-RED LEDGER. AUDIT_CI.md §5/RETIRE asked for exactly this instrument, by name: 'If declared known-reds must be carried, carry them as a machine-readable list keyed by assertion name — the tree already has the instrument (release_contract.json.held_checks), and it is currently empty.' This file is that list, living beside the runner that reads it rather than inside a contract another seat owns. An entry here does NOT excuse a red: it records that the red is MEASURED, KNOWN, and already before the owner or supervisor as a presented fork, and that no seat may clear it unilaterally. The runner reports such a row as RULED-RED (non-gating) and blocks everything downstream of the carrier, so one presented fork produces one row instead of thirty.
_schema_2: SCHEMA 2 (PLAN_v6 1a, 2026-08-20) ADDS STEP KEYS. Schema 1 keyed CARRIERS only — a named upstream fact whose coherence can be read off a file. 1a arms loud-red on WORKFLOW STEPS, and a workflow step has no carrier: keyed the old way it would match nothing, be reported stale on entry one, and red the runner for existing. An entry may now declare `steps` (workflow step ids of the form '<workflow>.yml::<step name>', or 'acceptance::<check name>', or 'script::<path>' for a proof retired from CI but still in the tree) INSTEAD OF or alongside `carriers`. Everything else about an entry is unchanged, and `stale()` now considers only entries that DECLARE carriers, so the two kinds cannot poison each other.
_probe_contract: EVERY STEP ENTRY MUST CARRY A PROBE, AND THE PROBE IS THE EXPIRY. A carrier entry expires for free — the carrier becomes coherent and the entry stops matching. A step entry cannot: nothing about a committed workflow file says whether its step still fails. The acceptance criterion this extension was built to (REVIEW_COLD_OPUS.md O1, verbatim): 'a workflow-step entry expires when its step stops failing.' So `probe.argv` is the command that asks the step whether it is still broken, `probe.match` is the recorded failure signature, and the runner reads four answers: the probe still fails with that signature (LIVE, the ruling stands); the probe SUCCEEDS (EXPIRED -> FAIL, retire the entry); the probe fails some OTHER way (DRIFTED -> FAIL, re-adjudicate); or a `heavy` probe has not been re-measured inside its own `probe_max_age_days` window (UNPROBED -> FAIL, nobody has looked). A probe must never write to the tree it measures — see tools/probe_bundle_equality.py for why that had to be said out loud.
_self_expiry: EVERY ENTRY IS SELF-EXPIRING AND THE RUNNER ENFORCES IT. An entry applies only while the drift it describes is still measurable. The moment the carrier becomes coherent — or, for a step entry, the moment its probe stops failing — the entry stops matching and the runner FAILS on the stale entry itself ('stale RULED-RED — retire this entry'). That is deliberate. A known-red list that has quietly stopped matching reality is the panel-10/10 failure mode all over again — the estate has retired four instruments for exactly that (the panel 10/10, the movers 'exactly two known-reds', the R14 fixture config pin, BOARD_MD5_GOOD). This ledger is built so it cannot become the fifth. It has already fired once in anger: see the R2 entry in `retired` below, which the runner demanded be retired within an hour of being written, because the fork it recorded was repaired upstream while this order was being built.
_how_to_add: An entry may be added ONLY when the fork is already presented in writing to the owner or supervisor, and `presented` must name the document that presents it. A red that is merely inconvenient, or that a seat believes is fine, is a FAIL. RULED-RED is not a snooze button — a drift nobody has presented reds the run, and that is the whole point. A red the record calls a one-line repair is REPAIRED, not entered here: PLAN_v6 1f carries all three recorded one-liners for exactly that reason.

entries.reason: the step asserts a fresh extract_board_view.py run reproduces BOTH committed UI bundles byte-for-byte. board_view_public.js does (105512 bytes, byte-exact). board_view_working.js does NOT: the regenerated file is 557956 bytes against the committed 558536 and drops the entire release{} block (release_version / balanced_board_md5 / engine_head / …). The extractor is not the sole writer of the working bundle — the landing act's UI writer adds the release block after extraction — so the step's premise is true of one bundle and false of the other.

probe.last_result: suite: PASS=124 FAIL=15, measured in an isolated workspace seeded from the checkout (docs/evidence/m1a_2026-08-20/oneliner_c_f1lens.txt, AFTER section)
probe._why_heavy: the suite needs a bootstrapped workspace AND a board built from it — ci-guards.yml runs it only after setup_env.sh + bootstrap.sh + rl_export.py + s4_matrix. It cannot run on a bare checkout, so it cannot run on every runner invocation, so the ledger demands a DATED measurement instead and reds when the date leaves the window.
probe._probe_environment: MEASURED 2026-08-20, with ACCEPT_HEAVY_PROBES=1 on the P1 box: the probe reports DRIFTED here, because /home/claude/rl_workspace is the STALE shared workspace (pre-D8 engine, pre-R23 store) and the suite dies at import on a missing vendor module before printing its 'suite:' summary line. That is the ledger working: the signature really is absent, and a probe that cannot start must not be read as a probe that failed the recorded way. The env above mirrors ci-guards.yml's step exactly; the suite still needs bootstrap.sh + a board built from it, which no P1 act will do on a shared box other seats are live against (M1a refused the same thing for the same reason). Hence cost=heavy and a DATED measurement, and hence the runner does NOT run heavy probes unless ACCEPT_HEAVY_PROBES=1 is set deliberately.

retired._note: Kept here rather than deleted so the ledger's history is legible. `retired` is NEVER read by known_red.py — only `entries` is — so a retired entry can never quietly go on excusing a red.
